earned_by: Disposable scoping on 2026-10-22, not evidence. On exact squares with the twist imposed along x, P(consistent) was 0.7153, 0.7122, 0.7090, 0.7091 at sides 32, 64, 128, 256 (100,000-400,000 samples; 1/sqrt 2 = 0.70711); the not-all-equal square pairs gave E_inf = 0.4993 +- 0.0011 earlier (NAE-INVARIANT-20261022-001B-E001). Untwisted squares gave P(no horizontal wrapping) 0.2452, 0.2462, 0.2475, 0.2505 (Newman, Grassberger and Ziff: 0.24999 +- 0.00007). On common random numbers the second difference of P(contractible) over the twist sectors was +0.0047, +0.0021, +0.0024 (+- 0.0010) on squares of side 32, 64, 128, within 0.001 of zero on 2:1, 3:1 and 4:1 rectangles, and -0.009, -0.038, -0.133 on squares sheared by 1/8, 1/4, 1/2. Directed horizontal winding on 64 x 64: positive only 0.231, negative only 0.231, both 0.287, neither 0.249. Twisted-long inconsistency fell with exponent about 0.20 (beta/nu = 0.19635). SC-TORUS-EXACT-20261022-001A-P001 proves the cone theorem: 3/4 means P(no directed horizontal winding) = 1/4.
question: At roughly five times the earlier precision: is P(consistent) on square tori twisted along one axis exactly 1/sqrt 2 (half a bit)? Is the untwisted one-direction wrapping exactly 3/4? Is P(all strong components contractible) additive over the two axis twists on rectangular tori? Does inconsistency with the twist along the long direction decay with the strong-component exponent beta/nu? What do other twisted shapes give?

public_inputs.model: uniform random orientation of the square-lattice torus with periods (Lh,0) and (s,Lv); a twist (px,py) is imposed on the double cover and the swap reverses arcs; topology of the projected cyclic edges (contractible, cross, winding class); 'consistent' means no cluster with an odd cycle under the twist
public_inputs.F_half: twist (1,0) on L x L: L = 64 and 128 with 7,000,000 samples, 256 with 3,200,000, 512 with 1,100,000
public_inputs.F_34: untwisted L x L: L = 64 and 128 with 6,000,000, 256 with 3,300,000, 512 with 1,400,000
public_inputs.F_add: the four twist sectors on common random numbers: 64 x 64 and 128 x 128 with 2,200,000, 256 x 256 with 800,000, 128 x 64 with 1,000,000
public_inputs.F_dir: untwisted 64 x 64 (400,000) and 128 x 128 (200,000): directed horizontal and vertical winding of both signs; 16 x 16 (20,000) for the replay
public_inputs.F_scan: twist (1,1) on 256 x 256; twists (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) on the sheared square (128,128,64); twist (1,0) on 256 x 128 and 128 x 256; twist (1,1) on 256 x 128; 400,000 each
public_inputs.F_small: twist (1,0) and untwisted on 16 x 16, 20,000 each, for the independent replay

definitions: Symmetrized estimators: for a twisted sector, P(consistent) = 1/2 + (P(even winding) - P(odd winding))/2 and P(contractible) = (P(contractible) + P(cross))/2, both exact in law by the duality; for untwisted squares, one-direction wrapping = (P(H) + P(V))/2 by symmetry. E = -log2 P(consistent). D = P00 - P10 - P01 + P11 for P(contractible), with the symmetrized form in twisted sectors, per sample on common random numbers. Standard errors from the per-sample variance of each estimator.

predictions.candidate_half_bit: fit E_L = E_inf + c/L by weighted least squares over the F_half sizes; accepted when |E_inf - 1/2| <= 3 sigma; decisively rejected when > 5 sigma
predictions.candidate_three_quarters: fit W_L = W_inf + c/L over the F_34 sizes (W = symmetrized one-direction wrapping); accepted when |W_inf - 3/4| <= 3 sigma; decisively rejected when > 5 sigma
predictions.candidate_additivity: fit D_L = D_inf + c/L over the three F_add squares; accepted when |D_inf| <= 3 sigma and |D(128 x 64)| <= 3 sigma
predictions.candidate_beta_nu: fit ln(1 - P_consistent) linearly in the aspect k over F_long; x = -slope/(2 pi); accepted when |x - 0.19635| <= 3 sigma + 0.005
predictions.reported: the short-side twisted exponent, the directed winding law, the scan values, and fits with an added 1/L^2 term
predictions.controls: every twisted row has zero disagreements between the swap-invariant strong-component test and the odd-cluster test and |contractible - cross| <= 4 sqrt(contractible + cross); for twisted rectangles P(no H) + P(no V) and 1 - P(lines in classes with both coordinates nonzero) agree within 4 standard errors; P(no horizontal winding) from the directed test agrees with the undirected value at the same side within 4 standard errors

decision_rule: If a control fails, the run is invalid. Primary: the two exact-looking values. Supported when the half bit and 3/4 are both accepted; refuted when either is decisively rejected; closed null otherwise. The additivity and beta/nu candidates are accepted or rejected by their rules and do not change the primary verdict.
stop_rule: Stop immediately if a control fails; otherwise stop after the frozen roster.
seeds: per job chunk: the integer formed by the first 15 hex digits of sha256('family|label|chunk')
environment: CPython 3 standard library for orchestration and analysis; simx.c compiled at run time with gcc -O2; 24 worker threads each running one subprocess
red_team_r0: Finite size: all three candidates are extrapolated with a pre-registered 1/L fit; a fit with 1/L^2 is reported as a robustness check, not a decision.
Estimator bias: the symmetrized estimators rest on proved identities (duality in twisted sectors; square symmetry), and the raw estimators are recorded beside them.
Leakage: candidate values enter only the analysis.
Multiplicity: two primary and two secondary candidates with fixed rules; scan values are descriptive.

Imposed twists: on even squares the twist is imposed rather than forced by parity; the scaling limit depends only on the torus and the twist class, which the not-all-equal squares of the previous epic share.
nonclaims: Monte Carlo estimates on finite tori; acceptance of a candidate supports and does not prove an exact value.
No formula for strongly-connected percolation is claimed.
Lattices are declared; nothing is said about space or physics.
forbidden_inputs: Scoping, published or candidate values as inputs to the simulation
